title: Annotation decision lab diary
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a personal lab diary for capturing ad-hoc labeling decisions, quick heuristics to try in the next round of guideline edits, and a handful of representative samples to use in reviewer calibration. Not intended as the final canonical guideline — think of it as scratch chemistry: small experiments, hypotheses to validate, and examples that repeatedly trip up the team.

Why I kept this separate:
- Too many tiny clarifications keep getting lost in the main doc.
- Want a place to record 'why' for some rules (rationales help when we revisit months later).
- Rapidly iterating: will move a subset to the official guideline once validated with 10 reviewer agreements.

High-level principles I want to preserve (for reference):
1) Prefer conservative span boundaries unless the application demands recall. If downstream system uses exact match, tighter spans reduce false positives.
2) Normalize entities at ingestion when reasonable (dates, currencies, commonly-used abbreviations) but preserve original text in the sample store for audit.
3) When in doubt, mark "AMBIG" and surface to SMEs rather than forcing a speculative label.

Open questions to decide in next sync (prioritized):
- Q1: Should we label embedded product codes inside descriptive text as PRODUCT if they are not fully standardized? E.g. "model: XR-42 (beta)" — label "XR-42"?
- Q2: Multi-language tokens: when a sentence mixes English and another language, do we prefer language-specific canonicalization?
- Q3: URLs with tracking params — should the entire URL be a single URL entity or should we trim UTM-like parameters and label the clean URL?

Quick heuristics to test this sprint (A/B list for QC):
- Heuristic A: Label only first occurrence of a proper noun in a doc as ENTITY_PROPER and ignore later repeats for span count.
- Heuristic B: Label every occurrence; use linking to relate repeats to same canonical ID.
(Goal: measure impact on token-level F1 vs downstream dedup recall)

Concrete edge-case rules (drafts):
- Parenthetical clarifications: If an acronym is followed by its expansion in parentheses ("NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)"), label the expansion as the same entity type but use the shortest span that is unambiguous (prefer acronym span for length-limited tasks).
- Hyphenated compounds: Label full compound if meaning is unitary ("self-driving car" -> PRODUCT); if hyphen connects modifiers rather than forming a name ("state-of-the-art"), do not label.
- Dates: Accept multiple formats as DATE ("2025-03-01", "March 1, 2025", "03/01/25"). Normalize to ISO in metadata but store raw span. If range present ("March 1–5, 2025"), label as one DATE span rather than two.
- PII vs Non-PII distinction: If a span could be PII but appears in a public user handle ("@john_doe") we should tag it as HANDLE and not as NAME unless explicit real-name context exists.

Representative samples and suggested labels (these are gold-like examples to add to validator tests):
1) Text: "Booking ref: AB-1234-XYZ (issued 12/12/24)"
   - Label: BOOKING_REF: "AB-1234-XYZ"; DATE: "12/12/24"
   - Note: allow hyphens and uppercase+numerics in pattern matcher.

2) Text: "We shipped the falcon-9a prototype to the SF lab."
   - Label: PRODUCT: "falcon-9a" (case-insensitive); LOCATION: "SF lab" -> normalize to "San Francisco" only in metadata, not span.

3) Text: "Contact: support@example.co.uk?ref=chat123"
   - Label: EMAIL: "support@example.co.uk"; URL/params should be split: URL_BASE: "support@example.co.uk" (note this is an email as a URL-like token). For URL-like tokens prefer EMAIL label if matches email regex.

4) Text: "He said 'we'll meet on 04/05'"
   - Ambiguity: Is this MM/DD or DD/MM? If no locale present, mark as DATE_AMBIG and require annotator to add locale hint if known.

Boundary and overlap rules (current thoughts):
- No overlapping labels of same type allowed. If two candidate spans overlap and are same type, prefer the shorter span (unless the longer span is recognized canonical name in KB).
- Allow overlapping labels of different types when semantically valid (e.g., ORGANIZATION + LOCATION if phrase contains both: "UN Geneva office" -> ORG: "UN" + LOCATION: "Geneva").

Normalization guidance (what gets canonicalized automatically):
- Dates -> ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) in 'normalized_value' metadata field.
- Currency -> ISO currency + numeric ("$5.60" -> USD 5.60).
- Units: Try to map to base SI if unit detected ("2km" -> 2000 m) but only for numeric-relevant tasks; otherwise keep raw.

Annotation psychology and friction notes: (things I've noticed during spot checks)
- Annotators tend to prefer labeling whole noun-phrases when given a free-form text tool. When strict spans are required, give explicit examples with token-level highlights.
- Overuse of 'OTHER' label when uncertain. Add intermediate label 'POTENTIAL' to capture low-confidence positives.

Sampling plan for QC this month:
- 200 random samples + 50 adversarial (long-form email threads, code snippets, social handles)
- Each sample to be labeled by 3 annotators; disagreement cases go to peer adjudication.
- Calibration goal: >85% inter-annotator agreement on canonical entity spans for the random set.

Mini checklist for labeling review (to paste into reviewer UI):
- Is the span minimal and sufficient?
- Did you normalize date/currency where required?
- Is this a real person/name or a handle? (mark HANDLE if handle)
- If ambiguous, did you mark AMBIG and add a short justification comment?

Ideas for tooling improvements (developer notes):
- Add a quick-toggle to show full raw text vs normalized view (helps spot normalization mistakes).
- Auto-suggest common canonical forms from the KB when annotator highlights a span (e.g., suggest "San Francisco" for "SF").
- Regex-based pre-label pipelines for ticketed patterns (booking refs, emails, order ids) but surfaced as suggestions not forced labels.

Follow-ups and experiments to run (owner: Maya):
- E1: Run 1K-sample pass with Heuristic A vs Heuristic B and measure token-level changes + time-per-label. Due: 2025-03-15.
- E2: Add 'POTENTIAL' label to annotation schema as a separate class and monitor false-positive drift. Due: 2025-04-01.
- E3: Build 30 calibration examples for date-format locale confusion. Due: 2025-03-08.

Notes to self (quick):
- Save newly validated rules into canonical guideline under page 'annotation-guidelines/v2/dates-and-handles' after E1 complete.
- Remind SRE to whitelist labeler VM for larger sample pulls.

Random heuristics that sometimes work (for brainstorming):
- If entity contains digits + letters > 60% digits label as CODE/REF.
- If token contains an @ or # and no space within token, prefer HANDLE/TAG over NAME.

Calibration example to add to test set (one-sentence, high-confusion):
"Transfer of $1,000 to John Smith via stripe.com/txn/342?utm=abc on 01/02/23"
Suggest labels: AMOUNT: "$1,000"; NAME: "John Smith"; URL: "stripe.com/txn/342"; DATE: "01/02/23" (marked DATE_AMBIG if locale unknown).

Closing note:
This diary is intentionally messy. The real value is quick capture and the institutional memory of why we picked a rule. Will formalize the top 12 rules to the shared guideline once we have consistent reviewer agreement.

---
Change log (recent entries):
2025-02-11: Created initial draft with common edge cases and experiments.
2025-02-20: Added heuristics A/B and three representative samples.
2025-03-02: Added normalization and tooling notes, calibrated sample plan.

Action items for next labeling sync:
- Present Heuristic A/B results (if completed) or propose timeline.
- Lock decision on URL vs email precedence.
- Approve adding POTENTIAL label to schema (2-week trial).
